specificationNote: This specification binds the one Virginia runtime route for Va. Code 19.2-392.2(I) and models its two branches separately: the court duty on statutory transmission under 2.2-402, which requires no participant filing, and the participant-initiated petition, which is governed by official Form CC-1472. It does not substitute CC-1473, which is captioned to subsection (A). It previously placed a custom 'Transmittal and Request' in the participant slot; that is superseded by CC-1472 and recorded under supersession. It grants no fulfillment or commercial authority.

statutoryAuthority.ruleStatement: Va. Code 19.2-392.2(I): upon receiving a copy pursuant to 2.2-402 of an absolute pardon for the commission of a crime that a person did not commit, the court shall enter an order requiring expungement of the police and court records relating to the charge and conviction; the order states that expungement is ordered under this subsection and is then treated as provided in subsection (K). That court duty is branch A and needs no petition. Where the participant is instead pursuing the filing path, the Supreme Court of Virginia publishes CC-1472 as the petition for this same subsection, and that is branch B.
doNotImport: Do not use CC-1473 or import the subsection (A) acquittal-or-dismissal petition procedure into this subsection (I) route.
Do not import subsection (D)'s Commonwealth notice period into this route; CC-1472's own service requirement is a copy on the Commonwealth's Attorney, which is a different thing.
Do not represent this packet as obtaining, classifying, or applying for the pardon itself.
Do not make the branch B petition a prerequisite to the branch A court duty.
Do not state or imply a fee exemption. Subsection (I) contains none, and CC-1472's own checklist says to file with all applicable fees and costs.

filingDestination.statement: Branch B: file the original CC-1472 with the clerk of the circuit court of the county or city in which the charge or charges were disposed of, with a copy of the absolute-pardon order attached. Branch A requires no filing: the court's receipt of the pardon copy under Va. Code 2.2-402 is itself the trigger.
filingDestination.office: Clerk of the circuit court of the county or city where the charge was disposed of
filingDestination.whyUnresolved: CC-1472 element 1 is a court case number the clerk may provide or complete when the petitioner does not know it, and CC-1416 is a cover sheet for filing civil actions where the clerk requires one. Neither source read states whether the petition opens a new civil case or is docketed into the existing criminal case, so it is recorded as unresolved rather than assumed.
filingDestination.sourceOfRule: Va. Code 19.2-392.2(I) and 2.2-402; current CC-1472 instructions

feeAndWaiver.statement: File CC-1472 with all applicable fees and costs, as its own checklist directs. Va. Code 19.2-392.2(I) contains no fee-exemption language, and no other current source read here establishes an exemption for this petition. The amount is set by the clerk of the filing court and is confirmed with that clerk.
feeAndWaiver.doNotDo: Do not record a zero amount, and do not tell the participant that this petition is free of charge or exempt from fees. The absence of a stated fee in the subsection is not an exemption.
feeAndWaiver.waiverStatement: No source read here states whether a fee waiver is available for this petition.
feeAndWaiver.sourceOfRule: Current CC-1472 instructions, filing checklist; Va. Code 19.2-392.2(I)

serviceAndNotice.statement: Branch B: serve a copy of the completed CC-1472, including its attachments, on the Commonwealth's Attorney for the county or city in which the petition is filed. Branch A prescribes no service, because it involves no filing. Subsection (D)'s twenty-one-day Commonwealth notice period belongs to a different petition route and is not imported.

hearingAndObjectionStops.situation: The pardon is not absolute, or does not say the participant did not commit the crime.
hearingAndObjectionStops.whatItMeans: This subsection (I) route does not apply; the packet does not classify or obtain a pardon.

hearingAndObjectionStops.situation: The court has received the pardon copy and has still not entered the order.
hearingAndObjectionStops.whatItMeans: The duty under subsection (I) is the court's. Take the pardon and the court's response to a lawyer or legal-aid office rather than assuming a petition is required.

hearingAndObjectionStops.situation: The clerk asks for a fee, a cover sheet or a filing step this packet does not describe.
hearingAndObjectionStops.whatItMeans: Filing mechanics vary by court. Follow the clerk and do not treat this packet as overriding them.

hearingAndObjectionStops.situation: A hearing is set at CC-1472 element 14.
hearingAndObjectionStops.whatItMeans: That line is the clerk's. If a hearing is set, take the petition and the notice to a lawyer or legal-aid office.

hearingAndObjectionStops.situation: The participant is still seeking the pardon itself or has an immigration question.
hearingAndObjectionStops.whatItMeans: Those issues are outside this packet's self-help scope.

participantChecklist.text: Confirm from the pardon document itself that it says both absolute pardon and that the crime was one you did not commit.
Check first whether the court has already received the pardon copy from the Secretary of the Commonwealth. If it has, the court must enter the expungement order without a petition from you.
Fill CC-1472 elements 4 to 9 from the pardon order, the court file and your CCRE record; do not guess.
Leave the court case number blank if you do not know it, and leave the hearing date and clerk signature lines entirely to the clerk.
Sign and date CC-1472 personally, or have your attorney sign, and select which role signed.
Attach a copy of the order granting the absolute pardon.
Ask the clerk whether that court requires a CC-1416 cover sheet, and what fees and costs apply.
Serve a copy of the petition and its attachments on the Commonwealth's Attorney for the county or city where you file.
File the original with the clerk of the circuit court of the county or city where the charge was disposed of.

branchModel.whyTwoBranches: Va. Code 19.2-392.2(I) and Virginia Form CC-1472 are both current and they do not conflict. The statute imposes a duty on the court; the form is the vehicle for the person who has to ask. A single instrument cannot serve both, and collapsing them is what this specification previously did.

branchA.name: Court-automatic, on statutory transmission
branchA.trigger: the circuit court receives a copy of the absolute pardon under Va. Code 2.2-402
branchA.rule: Upon that receipt, for a crime the person did not commit, the court shall enter an order requiring expungement of the police and court records relating to the charge and conviction, stating that it is ordered under subsection (I); the order is then treated under subsection (K).
branchA.doNotDo: Do not require a participant petition in order to trigger this branch, and do not present the CC-1472 petition as a universal prerequisite to relief. The trigger here is the court's receipt of the pardon copy, not a filing.

branchB.name: Participant-initiated petition on CC-1472
branchB.trigger: the participant, or the participant's attorney, is pursuing the filing path
branchB.governingInstrument: Virginia Form CC-1472, Petition for Expungement Filed in a Circuit Court - Absolute Pardon
branchB.doNotDo: Do not author a custom substitute for CC-1472. Virginia publishes the form for this exact subsection, so a custom document here is a substitution, not a gap-fill.
